title: Chengyu Catalog
blurb: A thousand four-character idioms, with pinyin, gloss, and — where coined verbatim in a classical text we ship — a link back to the line.
background: This is not a primary text but a reference layer over the rest of the library. Chengyu (成语) are the four-character idioms that condense a classical episode or quotation into a fixed phrase — see-once-think-twice, three-men-make-a-tiger, the fox-exploits-the-tiger's-might. Modern Mandarin uses several thousand; this catalog carries one thousand, curated for pedagogy and reordered so the most useful come first. Each entry has pinyin and a CC-CEDICT-sourced gloss; where an idiom is coined verbatim in a classical book we ship (Lunyu, Mengzi, Daodejing, etc.), the entry carries an `origin` link to the exact line, so reading 见贤思齐 jumps to Lunyu 4:22. Coverage is partial — about fifty of the thousand currently link to a verbatim origin — and grows as more classical texts ship; unmatched idioms simply carry no origin link. Originally derived from the MIT-licensed pwxcoo/chinese-xinhua list and rebuilt for pinyin + CC-CEDICT-only glosses; see tools/build_chengyu.py.

pedagogy_note: Pedagogy-first ordering: chapters 1-6 hand-curated core idioms by theme (study, judgment, action, collaboration, character, high-frequency story idioms); 7-20 continue from transparent/common toward more source-heavy and literary. 1,000 four-character idioms in 20 themed chapters.
provenance_note:
Curated 1,000-idiom subset. Idioms originally derived from the MIT-licensed pwxcoo/chinese-xinhua idiom list, reordered for pedagogy. Pinyin: CC-CEDICT where available, else composed from the per-character index. Translations: CC-CEDICT ONLY (no machine translation — the prior 3,000-idiom catalog had ~13% meaning-inverting errors from a GT fallback). 528/1000 have a canonical translation; the rest are honest gaps the platform's users fill.

Origin links: where an idiom is coined verbatim in a classical text we ship, the unit carries an `origin` link to the source line. Searched books (origin sources only — books that *originate* idioms, not just use them): Lunyu, Mengzi, Daodejing, Zhong Yong, Da Xue, Sunzi Bingfa. Sanguo Yanyi and the primers are deliberately excluded: they use idioms but coin almost none, so linking them would mislabel usage as origin. Coverage is partial (~50/1000) and grows as more classical texts ship; unmatched idioms simply carry no origin. Built by tools/attach_chengyu_origins.py.
selection_note: Stats: 1000/1000 with pinyin (100.0%), 528/1000 with CC-CEDICT translation (52.8%).
